# TabBar

Figma: [06b. TabBar](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-932) · Family: 06 Navigation · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-14

Two tab-navigation patterns built with atomic design: SegmentedTabs (in-screen underline tabs) and TabBar (bottom app navigation). 3 atoms, 5 organisms, full LTR + RTL.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/tab-bar/reference.png`

### TrendBadge

Small delta badge showing a percentage change with a green up or red down marker. Used beside a tab label, in portfolio table cells and anywhere a change value needs directional colour.

Level: atom · Part of: SegmentedTabItem, Table / Cell

Use when:
- Showing a performance delta on a SegmentedTabItem (HasTrend=true)
- Value change column in a portfolio Table (Table / Cell Type=Trend)
- Next to a Stat or KeyValue value to show change since last period

Don't use when:
- Status of a deal or issuance: use StatusPill or IssuanceStatusBadge (Investor)
- Category labels: use Tag

Accessibility: Do not rely on colour: keep the sign and arrow, and expose text such as 'up 7.6%'; keep the numeric run bidi-isolated in RTL.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Value | `value` | text |  | 7.6% |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | LTR, RTL | LTR |
| Tone | `tone` | variant | positive, negative | positive |

### SegmentedTabItem

One tab of SegmentedTabs: a 16px SemiBold label with an underline when active and an optional TrendBadge. Its state is driven by the parent organism.

Level: atom · Contains: TrendBadge · Part of: SegmentedTabs

Use when:
- Inside SegmentedTabs only; set its Label per instance
- Adding a delta beside a tab label (HasTrend=true)

Don't use when:
- Standalone: use SegmentedTabs
- Bottom navigation items: use BottomNavTabItem
- Pill-style value choice: use Segment inside SegmentedControl_2..5

Accessibility: role=tab with aria-selected; do not set State by hand inside an organism or it desyncs from the indicator.

| HasTrend | `hasTrend` | variant | false, true | false |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | LTR, RTL | LTR |

### BottomNavTabItem

One destination of the bottom TabBar: 24px icon stacked over an 11px label, brand colour when active and muted when inactive. Also the DNA reused by NavRailItem.

Level: atom · Part of: TabBar, TabBar (3-tab)

Use when:
- Inside TabBar or TabBar (3-tab); swap the icon and set the Label per instance

Don't use when:
- Standalone buttons: use IconButton or ActionTile
- Desktop side navigation items: use NavRailItem

Accessibility: Active item exposes aria-current=page; the label is always visible so the icon is decorative; touch target at least 44x44.

### TabBar

Fixed bottom navigation for the four-section Safqah app (Home, Investments, Wallet, Account) with exactly one active tab. The 4-tab IA is future: keep it in designs but do not wire into production until the IA ships.

Level: organism · Contains: BottomNavTabItem

Use when:
- Top-level app navigation on mobile, pinned to the bottom with safe-area padding
- Designs for the four-section IA (Home, Investments, Wallet, Account)

Don't use when:
- Current three-section production app: use TabBar (3-tab)
- Switching views of the same content inside a screen: use SegmentedTabs
- Choosing a value such as Day/Week/Month: use SegmentedControl_3
- Tablet and desktop: use NavigationRail or AppSidebar (shadcn-style)

Accessibility: Wrap in a nav landmark; active item aria-current=page; in RTL the first tab sits on the right.

### SegmentedTabs

Underline tabs placed directly below the AppBar to switch between two content views of one screen, such as Active vs Completed investments. Navigation-like (changes the view), not a form control.

Level: organism · Contains: SegmentedTabItem

Use when:
- Switching between sibling views on one screen (Active / Completed investments)
- Portfolio views that show a delta on a tab (SegmentedTabItem HasTrend=true)

Don't use when:
- Moving between app sections: use TabBar or TabBar (3-tab)
- Picking a filter or range value that updates the same view (Day / Week / Month): use SegmentedControl_2..5
- More than 2 to 3 options: use Select

Accessibility: role=tablist with tabs and associated tabpanels; arrow keys move between tabs.

| Active | `active` | variant | 1, 2 | 1 |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | LTR, RTL | LTR |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Page 06b houses two tab-navigation patterns built with atomic design: SegmentedTabs (top tabs with an underline indicator) for switching content views inside a screen, and TabBar (bottom navigation) for primary app navigation across Home/Investments/Wallet/Account. Both organisms are composed from small atom components - when the appearance of a tab needs to change, the change lives in the atom and propagates to every organism that uses it.

### Atomic structure

- ATOMS - building blocks each with their own variant axes for state, direction, and (where relevant) trend or icon.
- ORGANISMS - composed components that drop atom instances into a container and toggle each instance's state property to drive its appearance.
- Same pattern as Select (03d): Select Value + Dropdown Item are atoms; Select form field + Dropdown Menu are organisms.

### When to use SegmentedTabs

- Switching content variants on a single screen - e.g. Active investments vs Completed investments.
- Sits below the AppBar, above the screen content.
- Use 2-3 tabs maximum; for more options, prefer a Select component.

### When to use TabBar

- Primary app navigation - switching between the four core sections.
- Fixed to the bottom of the viewport with safe-area padding for iPhone home indicator.
- One tab is always active; tapping a tab navigates to the corresponding section.

### Anatomy

Both organisms wrap a full-width container around a row of repeated tab-item atoms. SegmentedTabs uses a label atom with an underline indicator; TabBar uses an icon-over-label atom with a color state. Editing an atom cascades to every organism that instances it.

### SegmentedTabs

- Container - full-width row, transparent fill, sits below the AppBar.
- Tab item (SegmentedTabItem atom) - 16px SemiBold label, optional trend badge.
- Active indicator - underline beneath the active item, bound to border/brand/primary.
- Trend badge (TrendBadge atom) - optional positive/negative delta beside the label.

### TabBar (bottom navigation)

- Container - full-width bar with safe-area bottom padding for the iPhone home indicator.
- Tab item (BottomNavTabItem atom) - 24px icon stacked over an 11px SemiBold label.
- Active state - icon + label switch to brand color; one item is always active.
- Item count - 3 or 4 tabs; distributed evenly across the bar width.

### Variants

TabBar ships three organisms across two patterns. Each is a fixed composition of atoms; the Active property selects which tab is current and cascades the active styling to that atom.

SegmentedTabs - in-screen tabs

Underline tabs for switching content views inside a screen (e.g. Active vs Completed investments). Two to three tabs, sits directly below the AppBar. The Active property slides the underline indicator and flips the label color.

### States

Tab items carry two persistent states - active and inactive - toggled by the organism through its Active property, never set on the atom directly. Pressed is momentary and handled in code; disabled is intentionally not a built variant.

Active

The current tab. Label and icon bind to text/brand/primary + icon/brand/primary; SegmentedTabs adds a 2px underline beneath the label. Exactly one tab is active at a time.

SegmentedTabItem

BottomNavTabItem

Inactive

Every non-current tab. Label and icon bind to text/muted + icon/muted; no indicator. Tapping an inactive tab makes it active and demotes the previous one.

SegmentedTabItem

BottomNavTabItem

> **Tip:** State is driven by the organism’s Active property (1–4), which flips exactly one atom to active. Never set an atom’s State by hand inside an organism instance - it desyncs from the indicator.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Every TabBar component ships in both directions via the Direction property. LTR uses IBM Plex Sans with left-to-right order; RTL uses Noto Sans Arabic with right-to-left order and right-aligned content.

- Tab order mirrors - in RTL the first tab reads from the right edge.
- Icons stay stacked above labels; only the horizontal order of tabs flips, not the icon/label arrangement.
- Active color and the underline indicator are identical across directions - only layout direction changes.
LTR

Left-to-right, IBM Plex Sans. Default direction for English content.

SegmentedTabs

TabBar · 3 tabs

RTL

Right-to-left, Noto Sans Arabic. Tab order and alignment mirror; the active tab here reads from the right.

SegmentedTabs

### Sizes

TabBar has no size scale - each pattern ships one fixed height and fills the screen width. The measured dimensions below are the source of truth.

### SegmentedTabs

- Height - 52px (hugs content); width fills the screen (390px reference).
- Label - 16px / SemiBold; item vertical padding 14px; inter-item gap 8px.
- Active indicator - 2px underline bound to border/brand/primary.

### TabBar (bottom navigation)

- Height - 80px content; 84px including the home-indicator safe area.
- Icon 24px over an 11px / SemiBold label; icon-to-label gap 4px.
- Item padding - 12px horizontal, 4px vertical; items distributed evenly.

> **Info:** No size variants exist. To change density, edit the atom once (SegmentedTabItem or BottomNavTabItem) and every organism inherits the new sizing.

### In context - common patterns

How the two patterns land in real Safqah flows.

### Switching content below the AppBar

SegmentedTabs sits directly under the AppBar to switch between content views on one screen - here Active vs Completed investments. The underline marks the current view; tapping a tab swaps the content beneath it.

### Primary app navigation

TabBar is pinned to the bottom of the viewport for top-level navigation between the core sections. Exactly one tab is active; the active icon and label take the brand color.

### Showing a trend on a tab

On performance screens a SegmentedTabItem can carry a TrendBadge to surface a delta (e.g. +7.6%) next to the label without leaving the tab row. Positive deltas read green, negative red.

### RTL - Arabic layout

In Arabic the bar mirrors: tab order flips right-to-left, labels switch to Noto Sans Arabic, and the first tab reads from the right. Build every screen in both LTR and RTL.

### Properties guide

Variant axes select the rendered state; instance properties fill content. Note: the organism does not forward a single label prop down to its nested atoms - set labels on each atom instance.

### SegmentedTabs · organism

Active  ·  VARIANT

Default: 1

Selects the active tab (1–2). Slides the underline indicator and flips the label to brand color.

Direction  ·  VARIANT

Default: LTR

LTR (IBM Plex Sans, left-to-right) or RTL (Noto Sans Arabic, right-to-left). Mirrors tab order and alignment.

### TabBar · organism

Active  ·  VARIANT

Default: 1

Selects the active tab - 1–3 on the 3-tab bar, 1–4 on the 4-tab bar. Switches that tab’s icon and label to brand color.

Direction  ·  VARIANT

Default: LTR

Same as SegmentedTabs - flips tab order and switches to the Arabic typeface.

### Atoms · instance properties

Label  ·  TEXT

Default: “Home” / “Active”

The tab’s text. Override per atom instance - cross-component forwarding from the organism is not supported (Plugin API limitation).

State  ·  VARIANT

Default: inactive

active | inactive. Driven by the organism’s Active property - don’t set by hand inside an organism.

HasTrend  ·  VARIANT  (SegmentedTabItem)

Default: false

Shows the optional TrendBadge beside the label for performance deltas.

Value  ·  TEXT  (TrendBadge)

Default: “+3.4%”

The delta string rendered inside the trend badge.

Tone  ·  VARIANT  (TrendBadge)

Default: positive

positive (green ▲) | negative (red ▼).

### Code examples

Reference implementations for the 4-tab bottom bar. Labels, icons and direction map 1:1 to the component properties.

```dart
SafqahTabBar(
  activeIndex: _index,
  direction: TextDirection.rtl,
  onChanged: (i) => setState(() => _index = i),
  tabs: const [
    TabDestination(icon: Icons.home, label: 'الرئيسية'),
    TabDestination(icon: Icons.trending_up, label: 'الاستثمارات'),
    TabDestination(icon: Icons.account_balance_wallet, label: 'المحفظة'),
    TabDestination(icon: Icons.person, label: 'الحساب'),
  ],
);
```

```typescript
<TabBar
  active={index}
  direction="rtl"
  onChange={setIndex}
  tabs={[
    { icon: 'home-window', label: 'الرئيسية' },
    { icon: 'chart-monitoring', label: 'الاستثمارات' },
    { icon: 'credit-card-3', label: 'المحفظة' },
    { icon: 'user-circle', label: 'الحساب' },
  ]}
/>
```

### Migration from Global_Design_System

The legacy navigation was Arabic-first and hardcoded. Syntropy v2.0 rebuilds it on atoms, adds LTR as a first-class direction, and binds every color to a semantic token. Mappings below.

Legacy: TabBar - 3 tabs (Settings · Account · Deals), RTL-only

→ TabBar 3-tab · Direction = LTR | RTL

Rebuilt from the atomic BottomNavTabItem. LTR is now first-class with English-default content and IBM Plex Sans; RTL keeps Noto Sans Arabic.

Legacy: no in-screen / underline tabs

→ SegmentedTabs (new)

New in v2.0 for switching content views inside a screen, with an optional TrendBadge for performance deltas.

Legacy: hardcoded active color and icons

→ Bound to text/brand/primary · icon/brand/primary · border/brand/primary

Dark mode and theme switching come for free once those modes are enabled on the Semantic collection.

Legacy: legacy icon set

→ Syntropy Icons (Streamline Sharp Line)

home-window, chart-monitoring, credit-card-3 (wallet), user-circle, briefcase-dollar, settings. Flag any swap that is not 1:1.

Legacy: fixed 3-section IA

→ 3-tab + speculative 4-tab organisms

The 4-tab bar (Home · Investments · Wallet · Account) is future IA - keep it but do not wire it into production until the IA ships.

> **Info:** This is a structural rebuild, not a reskin: the legacy single TabBar becomes two organisms (SegmentedTabs + TabBar) composed from three atoms, so visual changes cascade from one atom edit.

> **Warning:** Cross-component text forwarding is unsupported - a single label prop on the organism does not reach nested atom labels. Set each tab’s Label on its atom instance.

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Info:** Rebuilt 2026-06-11 using atomic design. Replaces the previous flat TabBar/SegmentedTabs (deleted). The atomic structure mirrors Select (03d): atoms with state variants composed into organisms.

> **Tip:** TabBar uses 4 fixed tabs (Home/Investments/Wallet/Account). For 3 or 5 tabs, add a "Count" variant axis or build a separate organism that composes a different number of BottomNavTabItem instances.

> **Warning:** SegmentedTabs currently supports 2 tabs. The trend badge defaults to Tab 2 - for variants that need the badge on Tab 1 instead, swap the SegmentedTabItem instance for the HasTrend=true variant.

> **Tip:** BottomNavTabItem icons can be swapped per instance using Figma's standard instance-swap (right-click the icon → Swap instance). The icon color binding to icon/brand/primary (active) or icon/muted (inactive) is preserved after swap.

> **Info:** TrendBadge is reusable beyond TabBar - drop it into Stat (04f), KeyValue (04g), CardDeal (07a), or any place that needs to surface a percentage change with directional color coding.
